nodes.title: Conductor parity of anticyclotomic characters
nodes.statement: For each finite continuous χ:Γ⁻→ℂ_p×, let c(χ)=0 for χ=1 and c(χ)=n+1 when χ first factors through Gal(Ψ_n/Φ), n≥1. Define Ξ⁺ by c even and Ξ⁻ by c odd. These are disjoint and exhaust the finite characters; conductor means the ideal p^c O, not the order of χ.
hypotheses: p is prime and p ≥ 5; Φ/ℚ_p is unramified of degree two, O is its integer ring and π = −p.
F/O is the Lubin–Tate formal O-module for π, λ its logarithm with λ′(0)=1, and T=T_πF is free of rank one over O.
Φ_n=Φ(F[π^(n+1)]), Δ=Gal(Φ_0/Φ), ω=κ|Δ, Γ=Gal(Φ_∞/Φ_0)=Γ⁺×Γ⁻; Θ_n=Φ_n^Δ and Ψ_n=Θ_n^(Γ⁺), with [Ψ_n:Φ]=p^n. Complex conjugation fixes Γ⁺ and inverts Γ⁻.
proofSteps: Use the local reciprocity conductor filtration of the specified tower, supplied by the missing Lubin–Tate interface G1.
The finite quotient Γ⁻/(Γ⁻)^(p^n) has order p^n; an exact order-p^r character, r≥1, has c=r+1.
